title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated device CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within an orchestration adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.01418, 0.07801]. We reconcile preregistration language and the formal estimand, report a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations (synthetic tasks, single model/validator). All principal numeric claims and per-episode diagnostics are archived in the study artifact bundle and execution manifest cited in the text.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored to translate operator intent into device CLI to accelerate network operations. While LLMs can produce usable drafts, they also produce syntactic and semantic errors (ordering, precondition violations, protected-resource breaches) that pose operational risk. Deterministic network-verification tools provide semantics-focused acceptance criteria and are natural candidates for deployment gates. Prior work shows promise for generate–validate–repair architectures but evaluation practices remain fragmented and often rely on token-level metrics that poorly predict deployability [1–3,6].

This study asks a narrowly scoped, operational question that was preregistered prior to execution: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The preregistered formal estimand is the paired difference in validator acceptance (guarded minus baseline) measured on a bank of synthetic adversarial intents under shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (single shared draft per paired test case). The experiment was executed end-to-end under the documented artifact bundle; numeric outcomes and per-episode validator traces are available in the archived execution manifest cited below.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic validators such as Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber and VeriFlow provide semantics-focused checks of forwarding and access-control invariants and have been proposed as deployment gates for configuration changes [5–7]. Their representational strength (explicit property checking) makes them suitable for deciding deployability, but they remain partial oracles dependent on the fidelity of encoded invariants.

Empirical studies of LLM-assisted NetOps show that model-only generation frequently yields topology, syntax and semantic errors; coupling generation with verifiers and localized repair reduces observable errors in prototype settings, but prior evaluations often use surface-match metrics (BLEU, token overlap) that do not measure validator acceptance or deployability directly [3,4,6]. Security analyses of LLM-integrated applications document prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks that can subvert orchestrated workflows, motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses [8]. Work on tool-assisted orchestration (e.g., self-supervised tool use) and generate–validate–repair patterns further motivates the present controlled study of guarded pipelines in NetOps contexts [9,4].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent a binary outcome equals 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; 95% bootstrap percentile CIs used 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729).

Design and task bank. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents; each paired unit comprised a shared initial generation and two downstream condition evaluations (Baseline and Guarded). Synthetic intent templates exercised administrative (up/down), MTU and VLAN updates with required sequencing constraints (shutdown–change–restore patterns) and protected-interface rules. The adversary model applied deterministic mutation heuristics to templates. Scope was limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded by the validator.

Model, validator, and pipeline semantics. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration used a generate–validate–repair adapter. The guarded pipeline applied a template-based input sanitizer prior to a deterministic verifier gate and permitted at most one automated repair call per policy. Because the preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate, each paired test used a single archived LLM draft per intent and then applied the two downstream condition-specific pipeline elements (baseline = validator-on-shared-draft; guarded = sanitizer ± permitted repair then validator). All execution and per-episode validator traces are archived in the study artifact bundle and referenced via the execution manifest [11].

Missingness and technical failures. The preregistered missingness plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). Provider-call accounting and all run-level artifacts are archived in the execution manifest [11].

Analysis. The primary analysis used the preregistered exact two-sided McNemar on complete pairs. Secondary and exploratory analyses (subgroup diagnostics, discordant-case tracing) were descriptive and used archived validator traces to attribute repair or sanitizer actions to paired outcomes. All analysis inputs and outputs are archived in the execution manifest and artifact bundle [11].
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting. The run completed 282 of the planned 300 episodes; 18 episodes failed for technical reasons and were handled per the preregistered missingness plan. After exclusions (paired exclusion only when both runs failed) 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis. Provider-call accounting recorded 156 model-call events in total, with 147 completed and 9 failed calls; the run invoked shared initial generation for each pair and repair-stage calls on a small subset of episodes. All run-level counts, per-episode diagnostics and provider-call accounting are archived in the execution manifest [11].

Condition-level outcomes and paired inference. Condition summary: Baseline successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085); Guarded successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar) yields p = 0.03125. The observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165 and the 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.01418, 0.07801]. These numeric results and the computed CI are archived and reproducible from the artifact bundle and execution manifest [11].

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant pairs (n10) are traceable in archived per-episode validator traces: in those cases the guarded pipeline converted an initial draft that the validator would reject into a final candidate the validator accepted. Conversion pathways included sanitizer-induced normalization/slot-filling and single permitted repair LLM calls. Repair activity is associated with these discordant pairs; archived per-episode traces show repair_applied flags for the episodes that invoked repair. Because the formal estimand measures validator acceptance-for-deployment, these discordant conversions increase guarded acceptance even when they reflect repaired benign drafts rather than direct elimination of attacker advantage. The precise per-episode diagnostics and provider-call traces for discordant pairs are available in the artifact bundle [11].

Missingness sensitivity. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. As a conservative sensitivity check (not the preregistered primary analysis), treating those 9 excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this conservative recalculation is reproducible from the archived missingness summary [11].

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and its planned false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are therefore reported. This omission and its effect on interpretive claims are stated in Methods and Limitations. The artifact bundle documents which preregistered secondary analyses were not executed [11].
sections.discussion:
Interpretive reconciliation. The preregistration's natural-language H1 asserted that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success; the formal estimand measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment. Our observed increase in guarded acceptance arises because sanitization and allowed bounded repairs recovered drafts that the baseline validator rejected. Thus the signed paired improvement in validator acceptance does not, by itself, prove reduced attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. To assess attacker-centric safety one needs an independent semantic-safety oracle or reachability tests in addition to validator acceptance.

Operational implications and co-design. Within the synthetic setting, sanitizer + bounded automated repair reduced operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. This operational benefit depends on (a) the validator's semantic coverage, and (b) careful specification of permitted repair scope. Repairs that blindly alter semantics could mask adversarial manipulations; consequently gate and repair policies must be co-designed with rich validator diagnostics to preserve safety.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size; the preregistered exclusion rule was applied. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences and protected-interface invariants but does not capture all dynamic protocol-level semantics; acceptance-for-deployment is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator and synthetic intents limit generalization. Conclusion validity: effect size is small against a high baseline (ceiling), so statistical detectability does not imply broad practical impact.

Reproducibility and protocol deviation. The archived model configuration recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (protocol deviation). To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call accounting; those execution semantics and all run artifacts are archived in the study artifact bundle and execution manifest [11]. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting the provider sampling parameter (e.g., temperature = 0) and re-running the archived manifest under identical provider semantics; the execution manifest documents the actual call accounting and resourcing used in this run [11].

Recommendations. (1) Execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle; (3) diversify generators and validators across vendors and CLI dialects; (4) fix sampling parameters (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction. Each follows directly from archived evidence and provider-call accounting [11].
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics show the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. Importantly, this formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliations above are supported by the archived execution manifest and artifact bundle referenced in the text [11].

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, CLI dialects, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
